audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike is described purely as 'one hook-into-R chain through your W shield'.
audit.why: Shields absorb damage, not displacement — Scrap Shield cannot stop Depth Charge's knockup or the follow-up stun. The spike is real but the stated reason is wrong, and the ultimate cooldowns (his 120/100/80 against your 130/105/80) were never given.
audit.corrected: Level-6 text now states that the shield eats the damage and never the knockup, and that his ult cycles faster than yours.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (W Scrap Shield: shield; R cd 130/105/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (a) 'Depth Charge travels ... through Scrap Shield's absorb on the knockup frame' invents a shield-piercing mechanic. (b) The single most decisive interaction in the lane is absent: Dredge Line is a projectile that collides with the first unit it hits, so a minion between you and Nautilus eats the hook outright.
audit.why: Rumble has no dash and cannot dodge a 1150-range hook on reaction; minion-blocking is the entire defence and the pages never said so. Meanwhile the shield claim teaches the player that W is useless at 6 when in fact it still absorbs all of the damage — only the knockup and stun get through.
audit.corrected: Shield line corrected in mid and whys[4]; minion-block added to early, wants.you[2] and the Don't entry. Staggering Blow named as the root that chains into the hook.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nautilus.json (Q Dredge Line: projectile, hardCC, range 1150; P Staggering Blow: first attack roots)

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line's cooldown is stated as 16 seconds in the early block and 18 seconds in wants.you[2].
audit.why: Both are wrong and they contradict each other. Real cooldown is 14/13/12/11/10, so the trading hole the player is told to wait for is up to four seconds shorter than advertised — they will step up into a live hook.
audit.corrected: 14 seconds at rank 1 used consistently in early, wants.you[2] and the cooldown breakdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentioned Titan's Wrath as the reason short trades stall.
audit.why: His W is a 12-second shield that also makes his autos deal area damage over time — trading into it wastes a Danger Zone window.

edits.before: At level 1 this is a feeling-out phase — Nautilus is melee and must walk to farm, so angle Flamespitter to tag him on every CS approach, but don't burn Heat to 100 for free. He has no ranged poke and his passive root only matters if he can auto you, so keep just outside his auto range while you Q. At level 2 the lane shifts in your favour: Q into Electro-Harpoon is a genuine threat, and Nautilus has no answer to the slow other than eating it. By level 3 you have the full short-trade loop — walk Q through him, double-E if he tries to walk out, Scrap Shield if he manages to hit back, and disengage as Heat drops. The one thing you must never do is stand still while trading: Nautilus's Dredge Line is a 16-second cooldown at rank 1, and if it hooks you mid-trade his full auto-passive root-E combo deals real damage even into your shield.
edits.after: At level 1 this is a feeling-out phase — Nautilus is melee and must walk to farm, so angle Flamespitter to tag him on every CS approach, but don't burn Heat to 100 for free. He has no ranged poke and his passive root only matters if he can auto you, so keep just outside his auto range while you Q. At level 2 the lane shifts in your favour: Q into Electro-Harpoon is a genuine threat, and Nautilus has no answer to the slow other than eating it. By level 3 you have the full short-trade loop — walk Q through him, double-E if he tries to walk out, Scrap Shield if he manages to hit back, and disengage as Heat drops. The one thing you must never do is stand still while trading: Dredge Line is a 14-second cooldown at rank 1 and it stops on the first unit it hits, so keep a minion body between you and him and the hook simply never reaches you.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are your strongest window in this lane — experienced Heat cycling lets you chain back-to-back Danger Zone Flamespitters, and Nautilus simply cannot sustain trading into that sustained damage without his Dredge Line landing. Keep the wave frozen or slow-pushed toward your side: he is forced to walk up to farm, which means walking into your Q cone, which means he is taking percentage-health poke with no way to retaliate cleanly. Track Dredge Line like a hawk — when it is down, commit the full pattern; when it is up, give him nothing and sidestep toward the wall to cut off his hook angle. At level 6 the dynamic flips briefly: Nautilus's Depth Charge travels under minions and through your W shield on the knockup frame, meaning a hook-into-R chain can go from full health to dead before Equalizer even finishes casting. Play 6 with your back to a wall so the Depth Charge bounce-chain cannot hit you from behind, and always have Scrap Shield ready rather than burning it for shield value on minion damage.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are your strongest window in this lane — experienced Heat cycling lets you chain back-to-back Danger Zone Flamespitters, and Nautilus simply cannot sustain trading into that sustained damage without his Dredge Line landing. Keep the wave frozen or slow-pushed toward your side: he is forced to walk up to farm, which means walking into your Q cone, which means he is taking percentage-health poke with no way to retaliate cleanly. Track Dredge Line like a hawk — when it is down, commit the full pattern; when it is up, give him nothing and sidestep toward the wall to cut off his hook angle. At level 6 the dynamic flips: Depth Charge travels under minions, and Scrap Shield eats its damage but never the knockup — the airborne stun is what kills you, and his 120-second ult cycles faster than your 130-second Equalizer. Depth Charge chases you, so a wall does not save you — stay near your own minions so Dredge Line has no clean line, and hold Scrap Shield for the hook rather than burning it on minion damage.

notes: _missing-interactions lists 'Both sides carry displacement (Dredge Line vs Scrap Shield)' and 'Rumble can cut your retreat with Scrap Shield, The Equalizer'. The Scrap Shield half is a derived-flag misfire: Riot's description is a shield plus a burst of move speed — it has no knockup and creates no terrain. I did not propagate it. The Equalizer half is real (it creates a burning wall) and is already covered on the page. Spell-shield, cleanse and tenacity behaviour against Depth Charge is not in the kit file and no claim was made.
